events.description: Najibullah visits Varennikov's residence for his birthday celebration; asks about operation against Masoud.
Shevardnadze and Najibullah conversation; Najibullah urges operation against Masoud before Soviet withdrawal.
Shevardnadze speaks at Soviet Embassy conference about operation against Masoud's forces; start delayed for supplies.
Yazov orders the 40th Army to prepare Operation Typhoon against Masoud.
Varennikov's 65th birthday; he had left for Kandahar a week earlier.
Najibullah attended Varennikov's birthday celebration at the Soviet residence and discussed the Masoud problem.
Shevardnadze and Najibullah conversed in Kabul; Najibullah urged action against Masoud before Soviet withdrawal.
Shevardnadze spoke at the Soviet Embassy conference about the operation against Masoud's forces and its delay for supplies to Kabul.
Yazov ordered preparation of military operations against Masoud; operation named 'Typhoon' with bombing and shelling of Panjsher.
Planned joint Soviet-Afghan operation against Masoud, limited to clearing areas near the road and replacing Soviet posts with Afghan ones.

relationships.detail: Najibullah sought a military operation against Masoud as the government's primary foe.
relationships.quote: Ahead Shah should be considered as the primary foe of the government for the time being.

relationships.detail: Masoud's group belongs to the Islamic Society.
relationships.quote: the group under Ahead Shah Masoud, which belongs to the Islamic society of Afghanistan

relationships.detail: Yazov ordered the army to prepare operations against Masoud.
relationships.quote: LCSF received its order from army general D.T.Yazov, the defense minister of the Soviet Union

relationships.detail: Conversation in Kabul 13 Jan 1989.
relationships.quote: excerpts of the conversation between E.A. Shevardnadze and Najibullah

relationships.detail: Najibullah joined Varennikov's birthday celebration.
relationships.quote: Najibullah arrived that evening and, together with Varennikov, joined in the celebration

relationships.detail: Masoud commands the party's forces opposed by Najibullah's government.
relationships.quote: they wouldn't have to fight the Islamic Society of Afghanistan Party's forces

relationships.detail: Masoud is the primary foe of the Afghan government.
relationships.quote: primary foe of the government

relationships.detail: Najibullah asked Varennikov to regard him as a third son, expressing close personal ties, and pressed for an operation against Masoud.
relationships.quote: I know you have two sons. So, please consider me your third.

relationships.detail: Lyakhovsky usually accompanied Varennikov on trips and handled his calls and visitors in Kabul; known him 20 years.
relationships.quote: I usually accompanied him on these trips, but this time I stayed to 'man the fort' in Kabul

relationships.detail: Varennikov traveled to Kandahar before his birthday, overseeing the security posts of the outer ring.
relationships.quote: Varennikov is in Kandahar overseeing the security posts of the outer security ring around the city.

relationships.detail: Varennikov was reluctant to rush back to a military operation against Masoud.
relationships.quote: it was not something he was hurrying to get back to

relationships.detail: Shevardnadze agreed that the operation against Masoud had dragged on too long.
relationships.quote: I agree that this operation against Ahead Shah has been dragged on for too long now.

relationships.detail: Gorbachev had dismissed the question of an operation against Masoud when the Afghan defence minister visited Moscow.
relationships.quote: M.S. Gorbachev already dismissed this question when the Afghan Minister of the Armed Forces visited Moscow three months ago

relationships.detail: Masoud's forces include 2,500 men in Panjsher.
relationships.quote: strike-force of around 11 thousand men, including another 2,500 in Panjsher

relationships.detail: Masoud's forces could operate from the South Salang region to blockade Kabul.
relationships.quote: across the southern Salanga region, and form a blockade around Kabul

relationships.detail: Najibullah blamed Pakistan's interference for the opposition's refusal of a cease-fire.
relationships.quote: continued interference in Afghanistan by Pakistan, the U.S.A., and other countries

relationships.detail: Shevardnadze was the Soviet Minister of Foreign Affairs.
relationships.quote: the Soviet Union's Minister of Foreign Affairs

relationships.detail: Shevardnadze said Soviet forces were ready to attack from 1 January.
relationships.quote: Soviet forces from January 1, and Afghan forces from January 5, have been ready for attack

relationships.detail: Yazov was defense minister of the Soviet Union.
relationships.quote: army general D.T.Yazov, the defense minister of the Soviet Union

relationships.detail: Yazov ordered the Soviet command in Afghanistan to prepare operations against Masoud.
relationships.quote: LCSF received its order from army general D.T.Yazov, the defense minister of the Soviet Union, to immediately prepare to commence with military operations

relationships.detail: Kryuchkov accompanied Shevardnadze in Kabul and left with him for Moscow.
relationships.quote: As soon as E.A. Shevardnadze and V.A. Kryuchkov left to Moscow

relationships.detail: Kryuchkov (KGB chief) traveled with Shevardnadze; KGB not named in text.
relationships.quote: V.A. Kryuchkov left to Moscow

relationships.quote: The command of the 40th army was not hearing any objections

sources_cited: Record of conversation between E.A. Shevardnadze and Najibullah, 13 January 1989, Kabul
key_claims: Najibullah repeatedly pressed Soviet leaders to destroy Masoud's forces before the Soviet withdrawal.
Najibullah claimed Masoud had a strike force of about 11,000 men, including 2,500 in Panjsher, and could blockade Kabul.
Soviet military command, including Varennikov, was reluctant to resume operations against Masoud.
Shevardnadze endorsed the operation despite earlier Soviet reluctance, delaying it only for supply deliveries to Kabul.
Defense Minister Yazov ordered preparations, leading to Operation Typhoon.
